# Phase 2 — Layout catalogue

Pick a layout by asking what *shape* the content is, not what the slide is
about. Two slides about completely different topics can be the same shape.

Every layout below exists as a worked slide in `templates/deck.html`. Copy the
slide, replace the text.

## Picking

| The content is… | Layout | Template slide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The deck opening | Title | S1 |
| One sentence that is the whole point | Statement | S2, S11 |
| What it looked like vs what it was | Two-column contrast | S3 |
| A sequence of phases over time | Timeline | S4 |
| A list of before → after changes | Change log | S5 |
| A list plus one thing worth boxing | Split + accent box | S6 |
| Steps in a system or process | Pipeline stack | S7 |
| Problems, each with a resolution | Problem/fix blocks | S8 |
| A quote and what followed from it | Outcome | S9 |
| Three parallel observations | 3-up reflection | S10 |

If the content matches nothing here, build the layout from the primitives
below rather than forcing it into the closest shape. A forced fit reads as a
template; a built layout reads as a designed slide.

## Shared chrome

Every content slide (not the cover, not statements) opens with the top bar:

```html
<header class="topbar reveal r1">
    <div class="sec"><i class="sq"></i>섹션 라벨</div>
    <div class="chrome"><div class="stages"></div><div class="pg"></div></div>
</header>
```

`.stages` and `.pg` are **generated by the controller** from `data-stage` on the
`<section>` and the slide's index. Leave them empty. Hand-writing page numbers
guarantees they go stale the first time a slide is inserted.

## Primitives

Build unfamiliar layouts from these rather than inventing new vocabulary.

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.band` | Accent-tinted takeaway strip with a left rule. One per slide, at the bottom. Optional `.muted` second line |
| `.chip` / `.chip.soft` | Boxed step in a `.flow`. Solid = emphasis, soft = supporting |
| `.arrow` | Accent connector between chips |
| `.pill` / `.tag` / `.lx` | Soft-filled inline item for unordered sets |
| `.label` / `.label.rd` | Small caps-ish section label above a region |
| `.stat` | Supporting figure line, `<b>` for the number |
| `.claim` | 38px assertion — a headline inside a column |
| `.quote` | Left-ruled pull quote with `<cite>` |

## The layouts

### Title (S1)

`.title-hero h1` takes a two-line title via `<span class="l2">`. Wrap the one
word that matters in `<span class="hl">` — an accent bar wipes in behind it.

The bar is positioned against the text baseline, so **check it after editing
the title**. Change the wording and the bar can land across the middle of a
glyph instead of under it.

`.meta` carries project facts — dates, duration, scope. Not the session's
run-of-show.

### Statement (S2, S11)

One sentence at 80px, line breaks placed by hand with `<br>` for rhythm. No
bullets, no supporting copy. `.rd` on the pivotal phrase; `.attrib` for a quiet
line underneath.

Use it when the point is rhetorical rather than informational. It is the only
layout that can carry a whole minute on a single sentence.

### Two-column contrast (S3)

`.cols` is `1fr 1.25fr` — the "before" column is deliberately narrower and
`.col-faded` drops it to 42% opacity. The right column carries `.claim` plus
`.tags`. Close with a `.band`.

The asymmetry is the argument: the faded side is what people assumed, the solid
side is what was true.

### Timeline (S4)

`.axis` ticks and `.steps` cards are two parallel 4-column grids. Mark the beats
that matter with `.hot` — accent tick, accent top border, accent numeral — and
leave the rest grey.

Highlighting all four defeats the purpose. If all four matter, this is a
different slide.

### Change log (S5)

`.change` is a 4-column grid: `210px | 1fr | 52px | 1.2fr` — area, before,
arrow, after. `.from` is faint, `.to` is solid with `<em>` for the accent.

Five rows fit comfortably. Past six, split the slide.

### Split + accent box (S6)

`.accel` is `1.15fr 1fr`. Left: `.acc-list` of numbered `.acc-item`s. Right:
`.acc-box` (3px accent border) for the one claim worth boxing, then optionally a
`.loop` flow and a `.stat`.

Use when a list has one member that is qualitatively different from the others.

### Pipeline stack (S7)

`.stack` of labelled rows, each a `.flow` of chips or a wrap of `.pill`s.
Solid chips are entry and exit points; `.soft` chips are intermediate.

Chips do not wrap — `white-space:nowrap`. Six chips at 25px is about the
ceiling before the row runs past 1680px of content width.

### Problem/fix blocks (S8)

`.blocks` is two `.block` panels on `--panel` fill. Each is: accent numeral,
`h4` problem, `p` why it blocked, then `.fix` — a rule, an arrow, and the
resolution in bold.

The `.fix` row is the payoff. Keep it to one line if you can.

### Outcome (S9)

`.outcome` is 1fr 1fr: `.quote` on the left, `.after` list on the right, `.band`
underneath.

`.after li` uses an absolutely positioned `::before` marker, **not** flexbox —
see non-negotiable #3 in SKILL.md. Do not "fix" it into a flex row.

### 3-up reflection (S10)

`.reflect` is three `.ref` columns, each with a 64px accent numeral over an ink
top rule. Close with `.closing-note`.

Exactly three. Two looks unbalanced in this grid; four is unreadable at this
size.

## When content does not fit

In priority order:

1. **Cut.** Most overflowing slides are carrying a sentence the presenter will
   say out loud anyway. Move it to `.slide-notes`.
2. **Split.** Two slides at a comfortable size beat one cramped slide. Slide
   count is not the constraint — attention is.
3. **Change layout.** A 7-row change log is a different shape than a 3-row one.

Never shrink the type scale to fit. That is the one option that damages the
deck in the room, where nobody can see that the body text is 20px.
